content: In Schatzmann et. al schatztmann2005effects cross-model evaluation is proposed to compare user simulators. First, the user simulators to be evaluated are used to train INLINEFORM0 policy each. Then these policies are tested using the different user simulators and the results averaged. BIBREF7 showed that a strategy learned with a good user model still performs well when tested on poor user models. If a policy performs well on all user simulators and not just on the one that it was trained on, it indicates that the US with which it was trained is diverse and realistic, and thus the policy is likely to perform better on real users. For each US five policies ( INLINEFORM1 ), each using a different random seed for initialisation, are trained. Results are reported for both the best and the average performance on 1000 test dialogues. The ABUS is programmed to always mention the new goal after a goal change. In order to not let this affect our results we implement the same for the NUS by re-sampling a sentence if the new goal is not mentioned.
